article.headline: A Feed That Rewrites Its Own Algorithm, Sourced From Wikipedia
article.lede: Most recommendation algorithms are static artifacts: trained offline, deployed once, updated through slow retraining pipelines. Surya Dantuluri's WikWok inverts this. His TikTok-style clone serves looped animations drawn from Wikipedia articles, then lets a language model continuously rewrite the feed's own ranking code — watching live engagement signals and pushing new logic into production without a human touching the pipeline.
article.body:
The content layer is the least surprising part. WikWok (live at quack.sdan.io, published April 2026, roughly 180,000 views) presents Wikipedia articles as looped *canvas* animations — programmatically drawn short clips, not recorded video — in a vertical-scroll interface modelled on TikTok's For You feed. The categories on offer include “Slop,” “Ducks,” and “Storytime,” a tongue-in-cheek taxonomy acknowledging the source material's heterogeneity. The Wikimedia Foundation supplies the corpus; Dantuluri's code supplies the surface.

The algorithm is the real experiment. Rather than a static ranking function, Dantuluri gave a language model access to a *REPL* — a Read-Eval-Print Loop, a live code-execution environment — and let it inspect engagement data (views, likes, scroll depth), write updated ranking logic, and execute it immediately. The result is a feed whose recommendation code is not a fixed model artifact but a continuously running agent: observe signals, generate new code, deploy, repeat. This sidesteps the conventional *retraining pipeline* — collect data offline, retrain the model, push a release — and collapses it into a feedback loop measured in minutes rather than weeks.

Holding the real-time layer together is Cloudflare (NET) and its *Durable Objects* primitive. Unlike ordinary serverless workers, which spin up in parallel with no shared state, a Durable Object has one canonical in-memory instance that is globally addressable from anywhere on Cloudflare's edge. WebSocket clients connect directly to it; when a view count changes, the object broadcasts the update instantly to every connected user. The algorithm state itself likely lives in a Durable Object too, meaning a freshly generated ranking function goes live globally without a redeploy.

Dantuluri describes his own formation this way: “I grew up in the Bay Area fine-tuning GPT-2 to do my homework.” His portfolio traces a consistent arc — NotRealNews.net in 2019 (GPT-2-generated fake news; 3.1 million views), ChatWithPDF in 2023 (briefly the most-used ChatGPT plugin; over a million users), and **Sudo** in 2025, a realtime website generator whose rendering pipeline WikWok directly inherits. He now works at an AGI laboratory and founded **Prava**, a company building computer-use models.

WikWok is explicitly unfinished — the project page trails off mid-paragraph with a bracketed note promising more explanation when time allows — but the underlying claim is legible: if a language model can generate code on demand, there is no principled reason to keep the recommendation function frozen between deployments. The hitch is trust. A REPL-armed model can push code that optimizes for narrow proxies — raw dwell time, outrage — while drifting silently from what a designer intended. The tension between self-improving efficiency and opaque objectives is not new to algorithmic systems; it just becomes unusually visible when the optimizer is running in a loop you can watch.

concepts.definition: A Read-Eval-Print Loop is an interactive programming environment that accepts code as input, executes it immediately, and returns the result — no separate compilation or deployment step required. In WikWok, the language model uses a REPL to run freshly generated ranking code against live engagement data, making the update cycle nearly instantaneous.

A Cloudflare serverless primitive that gives a piece of code a single globally-consistent in-memory instance, addressable from anywhere on Cloudflare's network. Unlike ordinary serverless functions that spawn independently with no shared state, a Durable Object acts as a persistent, globally-unique coordinator — ideal for real-time counters, chat rooms, and live feed state.

The HTML Canvas API lets JavaScript draw graphics directly to a 2D pixel surface in the browser, frame by frame, without pre-recorded video files. WikWok uses this to render Wikipedia articles as looped visual clips — dynamic, infographic-style animations — that mimic short-form video without storing actual media.

The conventional cycle for updating a machine-learning model: collect new labeled data, retrain or fine-tune the model offline, evaluate its performance, and redeploy. The process typically takes days to weeks and requires significant compute and engineering infrastructure — the overhead WikWok's REPL-based approach attempts to sidestep.

ticker_net.blurb: Cloudflare operates a global cloud services platform that provides security, performance, and reliability solutions for businesses. Its offerings include content delivery network (CDN), DDoS mitigation, web application firewall, bot management, and API security. The company serves a wide range of clients from small businesses to large enterprises and is a leader in the edge computing and cybersecurity space.
